News & Analysis on Domestic and International Trade, National and State Finances, Budget, Government Regulation, Monetary Policy, RBI Rates, Interest Rates, CRR, Indian Trade, Monetary and Industrial Policy.

item.title: Ind AS 118: India Inc gears up for big changes to financial reporting
item.description: India’s largest companies are preparing for the implementation of Ind AS 118, which may impact financial reporting. Changes include new classifications for income and expenses, and new operating profit reporting methods. Companies face challenges due to complex requirements and the need for system adjustments. Audit committees are discussing transition plans while awaiting final rules and guidance from regulatory bodies.

item.title: Competition Commission of India to hire 41 across departments
item.description: Individuals will be hired for positions at both CCI and its investigation arm, the director general (DG) office, according to public notices.

item.title: ‘Very high’ expectations from India-EU FTA, says Rotterdam port chief
item.description: Boudewijn Siemons, CEO of the Port of Rotterdam, expressed high expectations for the India-EU free trade agreement. He highlighted the importance of collaboration between ports and nations to facilitate global trade. Siemons conveyed his optimism about increased business opportunities between Europe and India. Negotiations for the free trade agreement have concluded, with hopes to sign it by year-end. The implementation of the agreement is anticipated for next year.

item.title: Cities cannot be governed from state capitals, need empowered local governments: NITI Aayog's Rajiv Gauba
item.description: Rajiv Gauba emphasized the need for reforms in urban governance during the National Urban Conclave. He highlighted the importance of empowering city governments and proposed directly elected mayors for better governance. The projected increase in India's urban population demands significant infrastructure and service management changes. Gauba called for improved municipal revenues and the adoption of the Model Tenancy Act to support affordable housing.

item.title: Cultivation of large cardamom emerges as a lucrative option for higher income from limited land
item.description: A farmer in Himachal Pradesh's Bilaspur district has cultivated large cardamom for 20 years, producing 2-3 quintals annually on about one bigha of land. Priced at around Rs 1.8 lakh per quintal, the crop offers an alternative income source for farmers with reliable irrigation, according to the agriculture department.

item.title: India's private capex pipeline surges 39% to Rs 99.7 lakh crore, risks rise: Report
item.description: India's private capital expenditure pipeline reached Rs 99.7 lakh crore in September 2026, marking a 39% increase. Manufacturing and electricity constituted the largest components of this pipeline, while the services sector showed rapid growth. A significant concentration of investments appeared in specific states and industries, with eight sectors accounting for 80% of the total. Maharashtra significantly increased its share of the pipeline, indicating a focus on regional development.

item.title: MSME business confidence improves despite rising input costs, manufacturing sentiment strongest: SIDBI
item.description: India's micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) are exhibiting a strong sense of optimism for business conditions, evidenced by an uptick in the MSME Business Confidence Index. The manufacturing sector specifically showed promising growth, advancing from 59.5 to 61.0 this quarter. Both trading and services sectors are also experiencing a surge in positive sentiment, suggesting a bright future for all sectors amidst ongoing challenges.

item.title: German companies plan to double, triple growth in India over 3-5 years: Piyush Goyal
item.description: German companies are planning significant growth in India over the next three to five years. Piyush Goyal emphasized partnerships in technology co-creation and skill development for Indian youth. During his visit to Germany, he met with various industry leaders to discuss investment opportunities. There is a focus on expanding German manufacturing and research capabilities in India. Promising sectors for collaboration include electronics, automobiles, and smart manufacturing.

item.title: India brings back duties on specified Chinese titanium dioxide imports
item.description: India has reintroduced anti-dumping duties on titanium dioxide imports from China due to material injury caused to domestic producers. This action follows a recommendation from the Directorate General of Trade Remedies, which concluded that Chinese imports were sold at dumped prices. The duties will be effective for five years unless revoked or amended. This decision comes after the Calcutta High Court ordered a reconsideration of a previous duty case.

item.title: FICCI seeks Dutch investment in mfg, tech; calls for project-level follow-up
item.description: FICCI has called for enhanced Dutch investments in India’s manufacturing and technology sectors during Piyush Goyal's visit. The discussions may lead to manufacturing partnerships and technology collaborations which would strengthen bilateral trade. Greater emphasis is placed on supply chain integration to meet Dutch quality and sustainability standards. The upcoming India-EU free trade agreement is expected to facilitate deeper commercial ties.

item.title: India, Uzbekistan discuss bilateral ties during foreign minister Jaishankar's Azerbaijan visit
item.description: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met Uzbek Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov in Azerbaijan’s Baku to discuss bilateral issues and stress the timely implementation of agreements reached at the highest level. The meeting follows Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s August visit to Uzbekistan, during which the two countries upgraded ties to a comprehensive strategic partnership and set a $5 billion bilateral trade target.

item.title: German businesses now see India as manufacturing, R&D and innovation hub: Piyush Goyal
item.description: German companies are increasingly viewing India as a strategic manufacturing and innovation hub for the future. During a recent visit, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal engaged with major firms about expanding cooperation. The India-EU free trade agreement is set to strengthen trade ties significantly later this year. Indian capabilities in research and development are attracting substantial German investment and workforce expansion.

item.title: Centre beats March 2027 target, issues 11 crore unique farmer IDs under AgriStack
item.description: The Indian government has successfully created 11 crore unique Farmer IDs under the AgriStack framework. This achievement was completed ahead of the scheduled deadline, enhancing transparency and efficiency for farmers. Farmers will only need their unique ID to access various government schemes and benefits. Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan highlighted the significance of this milestone for Indian agriculture.

item.title: India, Russia aim for $100 billion trade by 2030 as Modi, Putin push cooperation
item.description: Indian Ambassador Vinay Kumar announced collaboration plans between India and Russia to increase trade significantly. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Vladimir Putin have directed efforts toward enhancing mutual investments. India is ready to provide qualified workers to meet Russia's industry requirements by training specialists. The leaders reviewed these plans during their recent meeting at the BRICS summit in New Delhi.

item.title: India is not living in isolation, says Piyush Goyal, as India-EU FTA and several trade pacts pave the way for German R&D
item.description: Piyush Goyal emphasized the importance of collaboration between Indian and German research institutes during his visit. He highlighted the potential for co-development and co-innovation under the India-EU free trade agreement. Goyal encouraged the institutes to connect research with industry in order to support manufacturing in India. The minister also mentioned India's extensive trade agreements that will boost global market access.

item.title: Commerce minister Piyush Goyal discusses investment avenues with German companies
item.description: Piyush Goyal engaged with major German firms like Siemens Healthineers, Bayer, and Fresenius to discuss investments. He highlighted Bayer's plans for expansion and collaboration in India's healthcare ecosystem. Goyal also addressed opportunities for Fresenius to leverage India's talent for healthcare solutions. Furthermore, he explored ways to strengthen Siemens Healthineers' presence in the country. These discussions reflect India's growing relevance in the global healthcare market.

item.title: Private sector activity hits four month high in October
item.description: India's private sector activity experienced significant growth in October, reaching a four-month high as new orders increased. The HSBC Flash India Composite Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 56.7, signaling expansion. Manufacturing output and new orders remained stable, while services activity saw notable improvement. Employment increased slightly, although firms showed caution in hiring due to adequate staffing levels. International demand contributed to growth, with export orders expanding significantly during this period.

item.title: Target reached, but asset monetisation to continue: DIPAM secretary Arunish Chawla
item.description: "We have already identified a cluster of 10 national highways, which will provide the underlying capital asset. So, the second public InvITs is in the works and hopefully before the close of this financial year, it will also come to fruition," Chawla said. "We are also bringing down the equity (stake) in nationalised banks gradually to the minimum public shareholding norm of 75%, that is part of the mandate that we have to share the wealth with the people and also in line with regulations...we are moving ahead on that path."

item.title: Periodic Labour Force Survey to expand coverage to capture unpaid household, volunteers from January 2027
item.description: From January 2027, the Periodic Labour Force Survey will include unpaid household activities and digital platform workers. New questions will identify individuals engaged in caregiving and relevant unpaid volunteer work in both urban and rural settings. This expansion aims to enhance the measurement of labour-market data. The survey will enable better reporting and data collection on these aspects annually.

item.title: India to remain strict on quality: Industry minister Piyush Goyal
item.description: India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal emphasised a strict stance on quality and environmental regulations. He noted that many companies are eager to invest in India across various sectors. Goyal mentioned India's advantages in decarbonisation amidst competition from Europe’s carbon border adjustment mechanism. Discussions on free trade agreements indicate significant potential for job creation in India.

item.title: FSDC stresses on vigilance, reforms amid global uncertainty & AI boom
item.description: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman led an important session of the Financial Stability and Development Council, focusing on maintaining financial stability amidst looming geopolitical tensions and fluctuating global bond yields. Key topics included fostering a robust domestic investment climate, ensuring effective capital movement for reform, and addressing cybersecurity needs within the financial sector.

item.title: Strong macro fundamentals, policy interventions to anchor eco against global headwinds: RBI bulletin
item.description: Strong macroeconomic fundamentals continue to support the Indian economy against global inflation and trade tensions. Recent geopolitical frictions have resulted in increased prices and supply chain issues, leading to policy changes. Currency fluctuations were observed, but measures by the Reserve Bank helped stabilize the rupee recently. Foreign Direct Investment remains robust, driven by significant inflows from major sources like the US and Singapore.

item.title: India's exports to Germany could cross $50 billion by 2030: ASSOCHAM
item.description: ASSOCHAM said the potential for expanding market access, investment and business partnerships between India and Germany. It said the two countries could use their respective strengths in manufacturing, technology and innovation to deepen economic ties and create new growth opportunities.

item.title: RBI flags rising inflation risks from West Asia conflict, El Nino despite resilient Indian economy
item.description: India's external sector shows resilience due to a narrowing trade gap and comfortable foreign exchange reserves. Inflationary pressures have intensified due to geopolitical tensions and supply-side bottlenecks. The RBI reported an increase in both industry and services indicators, showcasing economic strength. The IMF has revised India's growth projection for 2026-27 to 7% based on resilient domestic demand. Global financial volatility has increased amid global challenges and rising inflation risks.

item.title: RBI's Rs 2.5 lakh crore liquidity infusion raises questions over tightening policy signal: SBI Report
item.description: In its report, SBI said the RBI had consistently signalled its commitment to monetary tightening through its policy resolution, the Governor’s statement and the minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC). The liquidity infusion through repo auctions, however, appeared difficult to reconcile with this approach.

item.title: PLFS set for fresh overhaul, govt seeks public & expert opinion on upcoming new things
item.description: The National Statistics Office (NSO), which has conducted the PLFS since 2017, plans to introduce the modifications from January 2027, when fresh samples for the 2027-2028 two-year period, designated Panel 6, will be drawn using an updated sampling frame.

item.title: Satellite lights, Google searches cut state growth estimation errors by up to 62%: RBI study
item.description: RBI study indicates that combining night-time light data with Google search trends can improve state economic growth estimates. Researchers tested their model in Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Karnataka, showing significant reductions in forecasting errors. This framework could help provide timely economic insights, as state data is often delayed. Night-time illumination proved to be a strong predictor of Gross State Value Added growth.

item.title: Inflation stays high, growth slows, central bankers face a bigger challenge, says RBI Guv Malhotra
item.description: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra highlighted the challenges faced by central banks due to global uncertainties and supply chain issues. He noted the elevated global inflation and lower growth forecasts impacting monetary policy decisions worldwide. India entered this phase with strong macroeconomic fundamentals, maintaining growth at 7.8% despite rising inflation levels. The RBI's goal remains to achieve price stability while ensuring financial market order and health.

item.title: India eyes 30 million tonnes fish output in 5 years, seafood exports of Rs 1.25 lakh crore
item.description: India has initiated a national action plan for inland small-scale fisheries to increase fish production. The plan aims to achieve a target of 30 million tonnes over the next five years. It will focus on improving livelihoods and sustainability amid climate change challenges. Stakeholder consultations will be conducted to finalise the plan, which covers diverse aquatic ecosystems.

item.title: Despite global tensions, India’s business sentiment rebounds in Q2 FY27: NCAER
item.description: India's Business Confidence Index has risen to 107.8 in the second quarter of this fiscal year. The survey included 502 companies across six major cities, reflecting both large firms and MSMEs. All four key parameters evaluated by the index showed gains when compared to the previous quarter. NCAER indicated that confidence improved in expectations of economic conditions and financial health.

item.title: India’s forex reserves fall $5 billion to $721.02 billion as of October 16
item.description: India's foreign exchange reserves fell by $5 billion to reach $721.02 billion for the week ending October 16. Previously, reserves declined by $8.578 billion to an amount of $726.027 billion. The decline in reserves reflects ongoing economic conditions impacting forex stability within the country. This trend indicates a continued volatility in India's foreign exchange market and its implications for the economy.

item.title: India’s labour survey to soon include platform workers and unpaid household work
item.description: India will update its Periodic Labour Force Survey starting January 2027 to enhance data collection. The modified sampling design aims to improve the identification of digital platform workers and unpaid household activities. Additionally, the updated sampling frame will reflect changes in urbanization and administrative boundaries. New questions will capture information on unpaid caregiving and volunteer work. Stakeholders are invited to provide feedback before the new sampling period begins.

item.title: Mozambique eyes India partnership to boost agro-processing, expand rice trade across Southern Africa
item.description: Mozambique is set to elevate its agricultural collaboration with India, tapping into mutual strengths in agro-processing. Secretary Antonio Do Rosario Grispos emphasized that India's rice imports are crucial for ensuring food security in Mozambique. This partnership aims to enhance trade routes via Mozambique's ports, fostering regional commerce and agricultural growth while strengthening historical ties with India as a strategic ally.

item.title: India must shift from rice volume to value, says Food Processing Minister Chirag Paswan
item.description: India has progressed in rice production and is now focusing on value addition and food processing. Food Processing Industries Minister Chirag Paswan outlined the need for improved quality and sustainability in the rice value chain. The government aims to enhance rice exports while promoting innovation in processing technologies. Strengthening agricultural links to industry is essential for achieving rural prosperity and increasing farmer incomes.

item.title: Piyush Goyal discusses investment opportunities with Bayer, Fresenius
item.description: Piyush Goyal held meetings with Bayer and Fresenius executives to discuss investment opportunities in India's healthcare sector. During these discussions, Goyal explored Bayer's expansion plans and potential collaborations in healthcare. He also examined how Fresenius can leverage India's skilled workforce for the healthcare market. Additionally, Goyal engaged with Knauf Group regarding sustainable construction materials and manufacturing operations in India. These meetings highlight India's growing role in global healthcare and manufacturing.

item.title: India October business growth hits 4-month high; hiring stalls, PMI shows
item.description: India's business activity expanded at its fastest pace in four months through a strong services-led pickup. The Composite Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 56.7 in October, exceeding forecasts due to increased orders. Despite this growth, hiring remained stagnant as companies managed workloads with current staff. Price pressures eased, resulting in lower input-cost inflation across both sectors. Overall, business confidence improved but remained below the average for the year.

item.title: Knauf Group to invest additional €350 million in India, plans four new plants
item.description: German building materials company Knauf Group plans to invest an additional €350 million in India to set up four new manufacturing plants, Managing Partner Murat Akyildiz said after meeting Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal.

item.title: MPC minutes: Two more interest rate hikes on cards, maybe even a third
item.description: Market participants and economists now expect a 25-bps increase in the December and February reviews. A further 25-bps increase in April isn't ruled out if crude oil prices remain persistently above $100. One basis point is a hundredth of a percentage point. "After the minutes were released, we think the probability of a consecutive hike in December has increased. Our terminal rate forecast is now at 6% for this hiking cycle and we expect the cycle to be rather shallow," Barclays said in a note.

item.title: Centre flags land, green tape hurdles in infra projects
item.description: Delays in land acquisition and obtaining various environmental clearances have significantly impacted the progress of infrastructure projects. Although central agencies are improving approval times, states are still facing lengthy procedures for necessary permits. Utility shifting is also causing major disruptions, often taking longer than projected. The recent analysis reveals a considerable increase in costs due to pre-construction delays.

item.title: RBI asks banks, payment firms to forensically clear tech environments in case of a data breach
item.description: The RBI has asked financial entities to remove management and administrative interfaces from public internet access, enforce multi-factor authentication for administrative access, and restrict access to cloud and backend systems on a least-privilege basis. The measures include auditing source code, repositories, configuration files, client applications and cloud storage for exposed credentials, and immediately rotating and purging compromised credentials.

item.title: Chana sowing holds key to pulses inflation
item.description: Chana, India's most consumed pulse, which is central to making everything from salty snacks to nutritious meals, needs adequate soil moisture and cool weather for a good crop. Sowing has started in some regions, but the progress is slow. State advisories to conserve water and shift to less water-intensive crops have added to concerns over winter sowing.

item.title: India-Germany trade can surge 10-fold, says Piyush Goyal
item.description: India-Germany bilateral trade is expected to increase significantly, with aims of reaching 310 billion from 31 billion. Both countries are focused on co-creating and leveraging their complementary strengths for economic growth. The India-EU free trade agreement is anticipated to be signed soon and will facilitate mutual benefits. Minister Piyush Goyal emphasized the importance of trust and cooperation between the nations.

item.title: GST return forms likely to be tweaked to curb mismatches
item.description: The government is looking to revamp GST return forms to minimise discrepancies between reported sales and tax payments. Draft forms will be available for public feedback starting November 1 and the changes take effect on April 1, 2027.

item.title: Berlin Global Dialogue: EU inviting disaster through carbon tax, says Piyush Goyal
item.description: Piyush Goyal expressed concerns over the EU's carbon tax and numerous regulations impacting their steel industry. He warned that these measures could lead to increased costs and decreased competitiveness for EU businesses. Goyal highlighted that the high import duties and standards could harm the economy and raise the cost of living. He mentioned the reciprocal nature of trade regulations in response to the EU's actions.

item.title: NSDC raises Rs 4 crore through Social Stock Exchange for global skilling initiative
item.description: The funds raised will be used to provide skilling and employment opportunities to 600 youth from economically weaker other backward classes (OBC) households in Madhya Pradesh. The programme, with an estimated outlay of Rs 11.25 crore, aims to prepare 600 candidates for international employment opportunities, with 300 candidates earmarked for Japan and another 300 for Germany, the ministry of skills development and entrepreneurship said in a statement on Thursday.

item.title: Parliamentary panel selects 25 subjects for review of urban development, Delhi projects
item.description: Under the Department of Urban Development, the committee will examine rainwater harvesting initiatives, legacy waste remediation, functioning of Smart City Integrated Command and Control Centres, and affordable rental housing projects.

item.title: India-EU trade deal could become operational in early-2027, Piyush Goyal says
item.description: India's trade minister Piyush Goyal announced that the EU FTA is expected to be signed soon. After signing, the FTA could be operational within four to five months. The deal aims to boost market access and bilateral trade between India and the EU significantly. Goyal emphasized the importance of collaboration in various sectors to maximize mutual benefits.

item.title: GST reforms from November 1 to simplify e-commerce seller registration, fast-track refunds
item.description: Starting November 1, the government plans to simplify GST registration for small e-commerce sellers. These reforms intend to reduce compliance burdens and facilitate faster refund processes. New measures will streamline registration by allowing sellers to declare e-commerce warehouses as their Principal Place of Business. Automated systems will issue refunds without officer intervention to improve operational efficiency. A minimum threshold for issuing show-cause notices will also be introduced to lower litigation.

item.title: China-Europe rail and India’s long road to Eurasia
item.description: India is focusing on connectivity initiatives such as the International North-South Transport Corridor and the IMEC. Geopolitical tensions have challenged India's ambitions to establish reliable connectivity with Europe. In contrast, the China-Europe freight network significantly expands trade routes across Eurasia. The expansion provides multiple routes and helps mitigate disruptions in maritime transport. A shift in India-China relations may further enhance India's connectivity options with Eurasian markets.

item.title: India's interest rate gap with G7 in focus as RBI weighs inflation risks: Report
item.description: India's monetary policy is now shaped by the interest rate gap with major developed economies and rising inflation. The Reserve Bank of India is concerned about inflation risks and input cost increases. Recent GDP growth figures indicate resilience supported by strong private consumption and exports. YES Bank predicts a cumulative rate hike of 50 basis points by the RBI.
